BiblicalUsage: Kelimmah means disgrace, shame, confusion: Job 20:3 says, I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer. Psalms 109:29 says let mine adversaries be clothed with shame, and cover themselves with their own confusion, as with a mantle. Isaiah 30:3 says the strength of Pharaoh shall be your shame. Ezekiel 16:52 says, bear thine own shame for thy sins, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe shame is a garment God can make the proud wear: adversaries clothed in it, Pharaoh's strength turned to it, Jerusalem told to bear her own. I hold that the only way out of shame is to bear it honestly before God.
